evals.prompt: Classify this with Cynefin before we write recommendations: our regulator just published a consultation paper on AI in credit decisions, no compliance practice exists yet, and our two internal pilots gave contradictory results.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Names exactly one of the five contexts with a reason keyed to the kind of causation; States the matching decision mode verbatim (probe-sense-respond for a Complex classification); Adds a one-sentence implication telling the reader how to consume the recommendations; Does not hedge between two contexts.

evals.prompt: Nobody on the leadership team agrees which kind of problem our platform migration even is — some treat it as a known engineering exercise, others as an unknowable mess, and the argument is stuck. What kind of decision situation is this and how should the team decide?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Recognises the situation as Disorder (Confused/Aporetic) when it is unclear which context applies; Applies the Disorder rule: breaks the situation into constituent parts and assigns each to one of the other four contexts; Does not take a decision from the centre of the framework; Reports each part with its own context and decision mode.

evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs a premortem on the chosen path rather than classifying the decision context; Produces failure modes, mitigations and a kill threshold.
